html:
The Lex Hortensia was a Roman law of 287 BCE that made the decisions of the plebeian assembly, called plebiscita, binding on all Roman citizens, patricians included.

It came out of a crisis. Weighed down by debt, the plebeians left the city in protest and gathered on the Janiculum hill across the Tiber, the last of several such walkouts, known as the secessions of the plebs. To bring them back, a plebeian named Quintus Hortensius was made dictator, and he passed this law.

It is seen as the end of the Conflict of the Orders, the long struggle between patricians and plebeians that had produced the Twelve Tables and the Licinio-Sextian laws. From now on the plebeian assembly, led by the tribunes of the plebs, could make law for the whole state. In practice a new elite of rich patrician and plebeian families ran Rome together through the Senate. But the law left a powerful tool in place: in 133 BCE Tiberius Gracchus used the plebeian assembly to pass his land reform over the Senate's head.
sum: The Lex Hortensia was a Roman law of 287 BCE that made the decisions of the plebeian assembly, called plebiscita, binding on all Roman citizens, patricians included.
